profile.headline: Software Engineer at Microsoft
profile.summary: I'm a Software Engineer at Microsoft.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Lead and develop strategic plan for reducing instrument obsolescence in the Automation Functional Test Equipment (AFTE) across twin-aisle airplanes (747/76/777), and introducing continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) to increase product quality and productivity.

Develop and support framework that orchestrates the execution of automated test scripts on Integrated Airplane Configuration (IAC) simulations through multiple 777X integration labs reducing hundreds of hours of manual lab testing.

Work as a part of the team designing the NextGen ATE architecture, which includes moving away from current monolithic design to microservices, as well moving towards cloud-based solutions, and providing a data pipeline to support data analytics. 

Support and develop 777X Automated Test Equipment (ATE) software to support functional testing and build verification, including interface for accessing airplane’s Common Data Network.

Support testing of airplane power, electrical and avionics systems, as well as communication interfaces for accessing ARINC 629 and 664 data networks.

Provide final assembly shipside support by troubleshooting software and interface systems associated with ATEs.

Lead data analytic effort for functional test data that includes data collection and analysis for predicting test failures and reducing troubleshooting time.

Support network communication and data pipeline process for ATEs.

Support mostly C++ and C# software applications.

positions.title: CFD modeler/ Researcher
positions.description:
Studied the southern shore of Puerto Rico and developed a high resolution (1/600 degree) ocean current model for that area using the Regional Ocean Modeling System.
Wrote Matlab, NCL, and Fortran programs in order to extract (1)initial and boundary conditions from Puerto Rico Regional Ocean Modeling System (PROROMS), tidal forcing from OSU Tidal Prediction System (OTPS), wind forcing from Puerto Rico WRF Model, and Bulk fluxes from Ncom AmSeas.
Validated currents and sea surface heights with NOAA buoys and mareographs.
Created a system that runs daily simulations (Pre-processing, processing, and post-processing) without human intervention using batch scripting and matlab.
Developed a similar model for San Juan Bay with resolution of 1/800 degree.
Wrote model documentation and full installation Guide that include all library installation and building from source code into Fedora (Linux distribution).

positions.title: Design of a Treatment Water Station - Student Engineer
positions.description:
Designed a Treatment Water Station for deep well water following Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) standards.
Studied water quality from deep well and Puerto Rico Aqueducts and Sewers Authority (PRASA).
Designed piping layout (pipe, fittings, and pump selections) from deep well to treatment water plant.
Reduced water cost from $9.0/1000 to $2.0/1000 gallons which represent an annual saving of 78% for the brewery.
Created a reliable system design that will serve as the primary connection of water supply to the brewery with higher quality controls than the ones of PRASA (City water supply system).
The design was implemented in the brewery.

positions.title: CFD modeling for Turbine Blade Cooling technique - Undergraduate Researcher
positions.locationName: Department of Mechanical Engineering, University of Puerto Rico Mayaguez Campus
positions.description:
Studied the effect of channel height-diameter and streamwise ratio on staggered pin fins with the purpose of avoiding damage to the turbine blades and stators cause by the extremely high temperature.
Ran Reynolds Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) simulation with different turbulence models (k-epsilon & K-omega) using ANSYS FLUENT.
Developed journals scripts for GAMBIT to generate unstructured and structured grid.
Validated the model solution with wind tunnel results from Penn State University.

positions.title: Design of a Autonomous Underwater Vehicle - Engineering intern
positions.description:
1. Managed all phases of the design process for components, assemblies and subassemblies, including dimensioning, tolerancing, prototyping and documenting results.
2. Developed a low cost design reducing  about $13,000 in the manufacturing process compared with similar Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUV)
3. Found a cost-efficient method of thrust generation providing the AUV the capability to change pitch, yaw and depth combining design and thrusting.

positions.title: College-level Tutor
positions.description:
1. Help college students develop their critical thinking and their capacity to organize their ideas coherently while writing.
2. Moderator of the Short Story Workshops in the campus.
3. Wrote the proposal for the International Spanish Short Story Contest that was accepted and sponsored by Title V Grant Program of the US Department of Education and the CIVIS Project. Designed and organized the logistics of the activity such as rules, requirements, judges and publicity. This was the first International Short Story Contest in the campus.
